minutes.headline: Committee unanimously recommended Article 11, funding a roof replacement over the central part of the TCP building at special town meeting.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the town manager and facilities director explain the proposed roof replacement over the central portion of the building, and voted by roll call to recommend Article 11. It then planned a brief project update for the special town meeting, discussed the RFP and cost-estimate timeline, and approved minutes from four 2022 meetings.

what_happened.line: The Municipal Building Design Committee voted unanimously by roll call to recommend Article 11, a roof replacement over the central part of the building, at the special town meeting.
The town manager and facilities director said the roof would be paid from money left in the fiscal 23 capital plan after the 30 School Street project, and a hard quote includes prevailing wage.
The committee agreed the chair will prepare a short project update for town meeting, with Mr Blat ready to present it and to say cost and timeline are being worked on before spring.
The committee aims to issue an RFP for cost estimates the first week of December, discuss it at the second December meeting, and make an award by the first January meeting.
The committee approved minutes from four 2022 meetings and set its next meeting for Monday the 20th, followed by the 4th and 18th of December.

why_it_matters: Article 11 is a funding vote residents will be asked to take at the special town meeting, and the minutes say it draws on leftover capital plan money rather than a new appropriation, though the amount is not confirmed here.
The RFP for cost estimates, which relies on ARPA funds whose disbursement has been delayed, sets when residents will see a price for the larger building project.
watch_next: The committee's next meeting on Monday the 20th, then December 4 and 18, when the RFP is to be discussed.
The special town meeting vote on Article 11.
